name: Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS)
coverage: national (state, CBSA/metro, county, and ~9,000 individual permit-issuing places)
granularity: county or permit-issuing place (finer than NYC's current NTA geography in principle, via place-level files)
license: Public-domain US government statistical data; no restriction found.
cost: Free. No documented REST/JSON API was found under api.census.gov (the EITS timeseries API's closest match, 'resconst', covers the New Residential Construction release, a different product, not BPS). The real access path is bulk flat files served from www2.census.gov/econ/bps/ (fixed-width/CSV by month, no key) or HUD's SOCDS Building Permits database (socds.huduser.gov/permits), which has a query UI/export and goes back to 1997.
history: Census.gov's own BPS files go back decades at state/metro level; SOCDS place-level monthly data goes back to January 1997 - solid depth for a permits-pipeline backtest.
integration_notes: Directly relevant to the 'development' pillar, which today is built entirely from NYC-specific sources: DCP Housing Database and MIH rezonings (app/sources/development.py, both NYC Socrata endpoints). Neither generalizes past NYC. BPS is the natural national substitute/supplement for 'pipeline_units_pct' and 'new_units_5y_pct' once the area-model migration happens, since every US county/place reports to it.
recommendation: Conditional recommend, same sequencing caveat as HUD FMR: it's the single most important source for making the development pillar work outside NYC at all, but there's no clean documented JSON API - it's bulk fixed-width/CSV files - so implementation cost is higher than a typical Socrata adapter, and for NYC today the existing DCP Housing Database is a richer, already-working NYC-specific source with pipeline/filed/approved/permitted stages BPS doesn't break out. Don't build this to improve NYC scores now; flag it as the pillar's path to national coverage and revisit when area-model generalization is actually underway.
